channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Germany enhance cooperation in state real estate management
item.description: An online seminar was held between Uzbekistan's State Assets Management Agency and German federal bodies to discuss state real estate management. Participants focused on Germany's experience, modern management mechanisms, and practical experience exchange. Cooperation in this sphere began in 2009, with Germany's BImA agency noted for its transparent evaluation and rental processes.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Attends Ceremony Honoring Victims of Repression
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended a ceremony in Tashkent's "Shahidlar xotirasi" (Memory of Victims) park to commemorate victims of political repression. The event included Quran recitations and prayers. Mirziyoyev emphasized the importance of remembering those who sacrificed for independence and highlighted ongoing efforts to restore historical justice and educate youth in patriotism.

item.title: Barskoon–Bedel Road Construction Faces Extreme Conditions in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The Barskoon–Bedel road project in Kyrgyzstan is being built under extreme conditions, including high altitudes over 4,000 meters, permafrost, glaciers, and avalanche risks. The 161-kilometer route, largely above 3,000 meters, presents significant engineering challenges. China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) is involved, focusing on safe transport corridor development and overcoming complex geology and short construction seasons.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's GKNB Disrupts Drug Trafficking Ring Supplying Narcotics from Afghanistan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has dismantled a drug trafficking group that organized an international supply and distribution channel from Afghanistan through Tajikistan to Kyrgyzstan. Two Kyrgyz citizens were arrested while selling 1.1 kilograms of narcotics. Further investigative measures are underway.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan extends ban on export of shell limestone
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet has extended a temporary ban on the export of shell limestone outside the Eurasian Economic Union. The restriction, effective for six months, applies to raw, crushed, or sawn shell limestone and stone blocks or slabs originating from Kyrgyzstan. The ban takes effect three days after the decree's publication.

item.title: Tashkent court resumes trial for businessman Sanjar Karimov, known as 'Real Sanjik'
item.description: The Tashkent city criminal court has reopened the trial for businessman Sanjar Karimov, also known as 'Real Sanjik,' and postponed the proceedings indefinitely. This decision followed the presentation of new evidence, including an audio recording, prompting the court to re-examine the case. Karimov pleaded for a fair verdict.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Proposes Candidate for Kurultai Speaker Position
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has nominated Aybek Dadebay, chairman of the "Adilet" party, for the position of speaker of the Kurultai. The proposal was made during the first session of the newly formed legislative body. The government will submit its resignation, and new appointments for vice-president and prime minister will follow.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Develop E-Parliament System Using AI for Lawmaking
item.description: Kazakhstan is developing a new E-Parliament information system to integrate digital tools for legislative work. President Tokayev instructed the Kurultai to adopt the platform, emphasizing the use of artificial intelligence in drafting laws to enhance analysis and reduce corruption risks. Strategic bills will still require expert review.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Reports 816 Infant Deaths in First Half of 2026
item.description: In the first half of 2026, Kyrgyzstan recorded 816 infant deaths, an increase from 781 in the same period of 2025. The National Statistical Committee report indicates perinatal conditions, congenital malformations, and respiratory diseases as primary causes. The Ministry of Health is planning reforms for perinatal services by 2030.

item.title: Mortgage Lending Drives Kazakhstan's Credit Market in First Half of 2026
item.description: Mortgage lending emerged as the primary driver of Kazakhstan's retail credit market in the first half of 2026. Housing loan volumes grew by 7.2%, reaching 7.5 trillion tenge. Consumer lending increased by 3.9% to 17.3 trillion tenge during the same period. Otbasy Bank led portfolio growth, followed by Bank CenterCredit and Halyk Bank.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Government Resigns Ahead of New Kurultai Session
item.description: The government of Kazakhstan has resigned, fulfilling a constitutional procedure following the election of a new Kurultai. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed the decree. The current cabinet will continue to serve until the new government composition is approved by the Kurultai. The decree took effect immediately upon signing.

item.title: Kazakhstan's construction sector grows, driven by state projects, analysts warn of dependency
item.description: Construction in Kazakhstan grew by 15.3% from January to July, primarily due to large state and quasi-state infrastructure projects. While housing starts increased by only 3.9%, engineering works like roads and power lines now constitute 54% of the sector. Analysts link this dynamic to government programs and infrastructure modernization.

item.title: Uzbek rowers win historic first gold medal at World Rowing Championships
item.description: Uzbek rowers Shahzod Nurmatov and Sobir Safaraliyev won Uzbekistan's first-ever gold medal in lightweight men's double sculls at the World Rowing Championships in Amsterdam. They completed the 2000m race in 6 minutes 21.93 seconds, dedicating their historic victory to Uzbekistan's 35th anniversary of independence.

item.title: Uzbek President to Attend Independence Day Celebrations on August 28
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will participate in the official ceremony celebrating Uzbekistan's 35th Independence Day on the evening of August 28. Earlier that day, he is scheduled to attend a ceremony honoring victims of repression and lay flowers at the Independence Monument.

item.title: HAS Pyramid Organizers Sentenced for Stealing 3 Billion Tenge from Kazakhstani Citizens
item.description: A court in Pavlodar has sentenced organizers of the HAS financial pyramid, who defrauded 515 Kazakhstani citizens of approximately 3 billion tenge. The scheme, active in 2022-2023, promised up to 70% monthly profit. Confiscated assets include land, apartments, vehicles, and cash.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces New Smartphone Registration Rules, Including Biometric Verification
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to implement new rules for smartphone registration, categorizing devices into white, gray, and black lists based on origin and IMEI checks. The system will include biometric authentication for registration and a separate procedure for devices used in detention centers and colonies.

item.title: Extreme conditions challenge construction of Barskoon-Bedel road in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Construction of the Barskoon-Bedel road in Kyrgyzstan faces extreme conditions including high altitude, permafrost, and avalanches. The 161-kilometer route, with 110 kilometers above 3,000 meters, requires advanced engineering. China Road and Bridge Corporation is involved in the project, highlighting the need for a reliable transport corridor.

item.title: Year-round mountain tourism complex to be built in Kashka-Suu village, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A tripartite agreement signed for the Baytik Mountain Resort project in Kashka-Suu village, Chui region, Kyrgyzstan. The $127.9 million project, financed by China National Heavy Machinery Corporation and Eldik Bank, will include ski infrastructure, hotels, and recreation facilities, creating over 2,300 jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan offers preferential loans for farmers adopting drip irrigation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture is supporting a project to introduce water-saving technologies, offering farmers preferential loans at 2% annual interest for drip irrigation. A total of 200 million soms is allocated for this initiative, with loans available for up to seven years, including a one-year grace period.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Orphan Housing System Fails to Provide Homes After Decades of Waiting
item.description: Over 43,000 orphans in Kazakhstan are waiting for housing, with many facing denial even after 18 years. A recent case highlighted how income checks now prevent orphans from receiving allocated apartments. Changes in housing distribution, with 'Otbasar Bank' taking over from 2025, have further complicated the process, leaving applicants uninformed.

item.title: Parliament's role in developing the digital technology sector discussed
item.description: Uzbekistan's parliament is reviewing its role in the country's digital development and the implementation of digital solutions in the economy. Laws on e-government, cybersecurity, and e-commerce have been adopted to foster digital transformation and improve public services.

item.title: Uzbekistan committees discuss improving public services and digital governance
item.description: Committees of the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis held meetings to discuss the creation of an integrated system for handling public appeals and resolving citizen issues. Discussions also covered the provision of state services at the mahalla level through the electronic government platform. Tasks from the "Uzbekistan-2030" strategy were reviewed.

item.title: Uzbekistan's independence fosters national harmony and religious tolerance, says MP
item.description: A Member of the Legislative Chamber of Uzbekistan highlighted that independence has enabled the nation to establish peace, interethnic harmony, and religious tolerance. The country is home to over 130 nationalities living in unity, with diverse cultures contributing to societal wealth. Constitutional guarantees ensure equal rights for all citizens regardless of nationality or language.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Deputy Criticizes Delays in School Equipment Procurement
item.description: A deputy criticized the slow pace of equipping schools in Uzbekistan, noting that despite allocated funds and deadlines, no new computer classes or electronic whiteboards have been procured. The Ministry of Preschool and School Education stated that 1350 computer class sets and electronic whiteboards should be supplied by the end of October.

item.title: Gastronomic Tourism Enhances Uzbekistan's International Image
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively promoting its national cuisine internationally through gastronomic tourism, viewing culinary traditions as key to national recognition. This approach leverages centuries-old traditions from the Silk Road and fosters international cooperation. Events like the 'Gastronomic Map of Uzbekistan' expedition attract visitors and boost the hospitality sector.

item.title: Kazakh President Outlines Key Education System Goals
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has identified crucial tasks for the education system, emphasizing quality education, fostering confident individuals, and preparing youth for the digital economy. He stressed the need for continued school construction to address shortages and called for reforms to be thoroughly analyzed for effectiveness, not just implemented for their own sake.

item.title: Presumption of Employment Protects Workers' Rights in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's legal system now presumes employment relationships, enhancing worker protection. This measure aims to prevent employers from circumventing labor laws by using civil contracts. Specialized judges are being appointed to handle labor disputes more effectively, addressing a rise in such cases and ensuring better legal and social security for employees.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Joint Production of Fuel with Azerbaijan
item.description: Uzbekistan has proposed to Azerbaijan the joint production of automotive and aviation fuel for Uzbekistan's domestic market, as well as long-term supply of oil and refined products. This comes amid Uzbekistan's interest in diversifying fuel sources due to rising domestic demand. Options include using existing refineries or participating in new Azerbaijani refinery projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan's economic growth driven by $160 billion in foreign investment over decade
item.description: Uzbekistan has attracted $160 billion in foreign investment over the past ten years, leading to a 2.5-fold increase in economic volume. This investment has funded 2,163 major industrial projects totaling $76 billion and created nearly 6 million jobs, according to state media.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to build year-round mountain-tourism complex in Kashka-Suu village
item.description: A trilateral agreement on public-private partnership has been signed to create the Baytik Mountain Resort cluster in Kashka-Suu village, Chuy region. The project includes ski slopes, cable cars, hotels, and restaurants, with an estimated cost of $127.9 million. Financing will come from China National Heavy Machinery Corporation and Eldik Bank. The project aims to create 1,500 construction jobs and 800 permanent positions.

item.title: Samarkand to host 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians in September
item.description: Samarkand will host the 12th Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians of the Inter-Parliamentary Union from September 4-6. The event is expected to draw nearly 300 delegates from 183 countries and 15 international organizations, focusing on youth rights and empowerment.

item.title: Kyrgyz farmers may receive preferential loans for drip irrigation systems
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry, along with the State Financial Holding, is implementing a project to introduce water-saving technologies. Farmers can obtain preferential loans at 2% annual interest for drip irrigation and other modern watering methods. 200 million soms are allocated for this initiative, with loan terms up to seven years, including a one-year grace period.

item.title: Uzbek President sends condolences to leaders of China, Nepal, and Pakistan
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has sent condolences to the leaders of China, Nepal, and Pakistan following natural disasters and a fire. The condolences to China and Nepal were related to landslides and floods in Tibet, which have caused over 350 deaths. Condolences were also sent to Pakistan regarding a fire at a medical facility in Islamabad that killed infants.

item.title: Uzbek-Chinese joint venture celebrates Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary
item.description: The joint venture "Asia Trans Gas" held events to mark Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary, uniting Uzbek and Chinese employees. The company highlights the strength of cooperation between Uzbekistan and China, particularly in energy, construction, mining, and logistics, emphasizing human interaction and mutual respect.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Singapore discuss mediation development and dispute resolution
item.description: Uzbekistan's Justice Minister Akbar Tashkulov met with George Lim, Chairman of the Singapore International Mediation Centre (SIMC). They discussed developing mediation in Uzbekistan and expanding mechanisms for resolving international disputes. Agreements include training programs for Uzbek specialists, exploring a regional SIMC office in Uzbekistan, and joint conferences to promote mediation.

item.title: 90 residents of Surxondaryo region granted Uzbek citizenship
item.description: In honor of Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary, 90 individuals residing in the Surxondaryo region have been granted citizenship of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Regional governor Ulugbek Kosimov presented them with ID cards, with one recipient expressing gratitude for peace and well-being in the country.

item.title: No Uzbek Citizens Reported Among Nepal Flood Victims, Embassy States
item.description: The Uzbek Embassy in Delhi has reported no information about Uzbek citizens being among the dead or injured in the recent floods in Nepal. The embassy is in constant contact with relevant authorities and monitoring the situation. Over 1400 people, including foreigners, are missing in Nepal and Tibet.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Visit Uzbekistan August 29-30
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will pay a state visit to Uzbekistan on August 29-30 at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Discussions will focus on trade, investment, defense, digital connectivity, energy, education, and humanitarian ties, aiming to set a future cooperation agenda.

item.title: Chuy Region strengthens river banks to prevent floods and mudflows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction and Ministry of Emergency Situations are overseeing river bank reinforcement work along the Chu River. The goal is to prevent mudflows, floods, erosion, and channel changes, ensuring construction quality. Work is nearing completion in some districts.

item.title: India donates $500,000 in medical equipment to Uzbekistan military polyclinic
item.description: India has provided $500,000 worth of medical equipment and supplies to the Military Security and Defense University polyclinic in Uzbekistan. The donation, part of bilateral cooperation, includes modern diagnostic and treatment apparatus, a specialized ambulance, and trauma equipment.
